definitions.explanation: Behavior characterized by doing what one wants without considering others; selfishness or capriciousness.

examples.japanese: わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}わないで→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Don't be selfish. / Don't make selfish demands.
examples.notes: わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧ = to make selfish demands

examples.japanese: わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{許|ゆる}してください→許す：02325_yurusu⟧。
examples.notes: Often used apologetically when making a personal request

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧わがまま⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{思|おも}い{通|どお}り→思い通り：25845_omoidoori⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦したがる→したがる：noentry⟧。
examples.english: That person is selfish and always wants things to go their own way.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{何|なん}でも→何でも：00304_nandemo⟧⟦{聞|き}いていると→聞く：00483_kiku⟧、⟦{大人|おとな}→大人：02856_otona⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なってから→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{困|こま}ることになる→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: If you give in to every selfish demand a child makes, it will cause problems when they grow up.
examples.notes: わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧ = to give in to selfish demands

notes:
わがまま describes putting one's own wishes ahead of everyone else's — selfish, self-indulgent, wilful. It is used constantly of children who will not do as they are told, and of adults who behave the same way.

It is both a na-adjective and a noun. As a noun it names the selfish behaviour itself, which is why it takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ and a verb: わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧ is literally 'to say a selfishness,' i.e. to make demands one has no right to make.

Common patterns:
- わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to make selfish demands
- わがまま⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a selfish person
- わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}す→通す：02300_toosu⟧: to get one's own way

Register: usually a criticism, but it is very often turned on oneself as a softener — わがまま⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}って→言う：00515_iu⟧すみません, 'sorry to be difficult,' is a normal way to preface an inconvenient request. Said of a child it is mild; said flatly of an adult it stings.

Similar words: ⟦{自分勝手|じぶんかって}→自分勝手：19490_jibunkatte⟧ is blunter and purely critical, with none of わがまま's affectionate or self-deprecating uses. The opposite quality is ⟦{素直|すなお}→素直：00391_sunao⟧, being frank and unresisting.

Orthography: usually written in hiragana; the kanji {我儘|わがまま} exists but is uncommon.
